why: Each territory's two source shares sum to 100% (negative where spend per customer fell), and annual growth of 1.5% to 5.3% is believable for a software reseller.

Copy prices of EUR 0.06 to 0.09 a page, a few hundred customers per shop a week and EUR 3 of stationery each are believable, and a 25% stationery margin against 10% for the market is within a factor of a few.
A low-cost airline selling 600,000 wraps a year at $7.00, bought at $4.00 to $4.30 with $2.50 of handling, is believable.
The eight sources sum exactly to the 19.7 million tonne total, a believable figure for a large city.
The group member counts add to the stated 122k, and GBP 11.2 million of cost over 1.8 million loans (about 15 per member) is believable for a 14-branch city library service.
Half-year spend of $52 to $129 per client at a budget salon chain is believable, and the question's drop/growth is a stated hypothetical.
Delisting probabilities of 10% to 40% and $3 to $14 million of annual profit at risk per chain are believable for a snack and drinks maker.
Each survey row is a subset no larger than the one above it for both medical (846 to 214) and dental (573 to 65) practices, so the funnel is consistent.
Byteguard's shares of about 7% to 8% in cloud backup and about 22% to 25% in antivirus are believable for a vendor with roughly $500 million revenue.
Strike probabilities of 10% to 50% and costs of $1 to $18 million per staff group are believable for an airline of unstated size.
